intro.heading: The manager says it is all fine. How would you know?
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: You bought the business, or inherited it, and your background is finance, property or running other companies. Your registered manager is capable and works hard. When you ask how things are, the answer is "fine", and you have no way to test it. You are not being nosy. You are the person the regulator will look to, and you want a few plain numbers you can read in ten minutes, the same way every week, without needing a clinical vocabulary. Here is how that usually plays out.

trail.text: The manager reports that audits are on track and staff are doing well.
You trust her, and you have no reason not to.
You ask for a copy of the audits and receive a folder of forms.
Nobody has added up the scores, so you cannot see whether they are rising or falling.
You cannot tell which are late, which were skipped and which repeat the same failure.
Actions were raised, but you cannot see which are still open or who owns them.
No one can tell you which questions staff keep getting wrong.
An inspector asks how you, as owner, know the service is safe.

trail_close: Trust is fine. Trust with nothing to check is the risk. Here is what CareStream puts in front of an owner each week, and what it deliberately does not claim to tell you.

why.heading: Governance is about how you know, not what you hope
why.sub: Regulation 17 of the 2014 regulations requires systems or processes that assess, monitor and improve the quality and safety of the service. Owners need to see those systems working.

cards.title: "Fine" is not a figure
cards.body: A manager can be right and still unable to prove it. A score by month, or a list of overdue audits, turns a feeling into something you can both discuss.

cards.title: You need a rhythm, not a login habit
cards.body: A weekly email that arrives on its own is easier to keep up than a dashboard you have to remember to open.

cards.title: Late and missed work hides in the gaps
cards.body: A skipped audit leaves no paperwork behind it. It only shows up when something records that it was due and did not happen.

talk.heading: The questions owners ask, and how CareStream answers them

items.q: I am not clinical. What can I actually look at?
items.a: Four things, in plain words: audit scores by month, which audits are overdue or missed, which actions are still open, and the knowledge gaps digest on Mondays. None of them need clinical knowledge. They answer "is the routine running, and is it getting better or worse?"

items.q: What do I need to do to see it?
items.a: Ask your manager to give you an "Admin, full access" login under Staff. Insights and the scheduling controls are for admins. Then check your email preferences in Settings, so the Monday digest and the audit summary reach you.

items.q: Does the Monday email cover everything?
items.a: No, and it is worth knowing. The Monday digest is about knowledge gaps only: open gaps, staff affected, closed this week and engaged with learning. Audit information comes in a separate summary email, which you can set to daily, weekly or off in Settings.

items.q: How does a knowledge gap get there in the first place?
items.a: Your manager allocates adhoc training built from your policies. A carer who answers wrongly gets a follow up in the Staff Hub, and chooses Learn & retry or Just retry. The gap closes when they get it right, and you see the totals.

items.q: Will I be told every time someone gets a question wrong?
items.a: No. Nothing alerts you on each wrong answer. You see the pattern in the digest and in the Knowledge gaps view. That keeps the picture calm and useful rather than noisy.

items.q: Can I trust a score of 90 per cent?
items.a: Trust it as what it is: the share of checks met in the audits that were completed. It shows activity and results. It cannot tell you whether care feels kind. For that you still visit, sit with residents and ask staff what they would do.

items.q: Is this a rating or a CQC record?
items.a: No. CareStream is software your service uses to run audits, training and follow up. It is not a pass, a rating or a regulator record. Think of it as your own paper trail, tidier and easier to read.

There is a 14 day free trial. Create a free account, add your manager as an admin, and run one audit from the library. Audits are included on every plan, so you can see the owner view quickly. See the pricing page for what each plan includes.

limits.heading: A window onto the routine, not a replacement for you

cards.title: It shows activity, not quality of care
cards.body: Scores, overdue lists and gaps show what was done and what was found. They do not show how a resident felt at lunch. You still need to visit and talk to staff.

cards.title: Some views are for admins only
cards.body: Insights and scheduling controls need an admin login. The Monday digest goes to admins, and the audit summary email goes to admins, so an owner who wants either needs that access.

cards.title: No alert for every slip, and some emails hold back
cards.body: Nothing tells you each time a carer gets a question wrong, and the digest only sends when there is something to report. Check which plan includes adhoc training and translation on the pricing page.

faqs.heading: Owner questions about care home compliance, answered

items.q: What should a care home owner check each week?
items.a: Keep it to a few things: audit scores by month, overdue and missed audits, open actions and the knowledge gaps digest. The dashboard nobody opens is a common trap, so pick a small list and stick to it.

items.q: What is care home governance in plain words?
items.a: It is the set of checks and routines that let the people in charge know how the service is doing and act on it. Regulation 17 expects systems that assess, monitor and improve quality and safety. CareStream gives you a visible record of that routine.

items.q: Do directors have their own duties?
items.a: Yes. For example, regulation 5 deals with the fit and proper person requirements for directors of a provider. Software does not meet that duty for you, but it can help you stay informed.

items.q: Can an owner see the data without being a manager?
items.a: Yes, with an "Admin, full access" login. Your manager sets the access level under Staff. See how CareStream works for the wider picture.

items.q: Is care home compliance software the same as a rating?
items.a: No. It helps you run and record your own checks. It is not a pass, a rating or a regulator record. See CQC and compliance for what it helps you evidence.

The built in audit library, scoring, scheduling and action tracking are included on every plan. Some extras, such as draft recommendations and the action plan draft, are on paid plans. See the pricing page.

items.q: How does CareStream help with care home compliance across staff knowledge?
items.a: Your manager allocates adhoc training from your policies, and wrong answers become short follow up lessons that you see as knowledge gaps.
Group views exist for accounts with more than one site, but plan details differ. See the pricing page for which plan includes them.

guide.heading: A ten minute Monday routine for an owner who is not clinical
guide.lede: You do not need clinical language to practise good care home governance. You need the same few questions, asked at the same time, with something in front of you.

sections.h3: Start with the things that arrive on their own
paragraphs: Open the Monday digest and the audit summary email first. They come to you, so the routine does not depend on remembering a login. Note the numbers and compare them with last week. Is the open gaps figure down? Is anything overdue? Write one question for your manager from what you see, and ask it with curiosity rather than suspicion.
checklist: Read the Monday knowledge gaps digest and note open gaps and staff affected
Read the audit summary email: what is overdue, due soon and completed
Open the Audits page, Insights, and look at the score by month for two audits
Write one question for your manager, about a topic or an audit, not a person

paragraphs: A weekly picture is a prompt, not a verdict. Once a month, walk the home, sit with a resident, and ask a carer what they would do if someone told them something worrying. If the answers match what the figures suggest, you have learned something. If they do not, you have found the question to ask. For the legal side, regulation 17 is the place to start reading about governance duties.
